chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Ṣafwān, from Shuʿayb, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who accused his wife, and then they engaged in mutual imprecation, then after they had separated he again accused her of zina. Is there a hadd upon him? He said: “Yes, there is a hadd upon him.”

key_terms.امْرَأَتَهُ: His wife, the woman he was married to.
key_terms.تَفَرَّقَا: The two separated from one another.
key_terms.فَتَلَاعَنَا: The two engaged in liʿān, mutual imprecation between spouses.

ai.seo_question: If a husband accuses his wife of zina again after liʿān and separation, is he subject to the hadd?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a husband who had already entered into liʿān with his wife and then, after their separation, again accused her of zina. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that the legal punishment for false accusation applies to him in that case.
